output.name: Haku
output.myth: Aun told the boy about the ribbon, and Aun never says a true thing without a joke in it, so the boy heard only the joke. The girl had dropped her float off the Windward ledge and promised her grandmother's cloth to whoever brought it back. He folded his arms and dropped like a thrown gaff, past Orrun's back and Kael's empty net, and found nothing down there but salt. He came up with his mouth full of it. The girl laughed. Tavo laughed louder and blew the spray off him. Ennu saw him dripping on the rock and carved him a gannet called Haku, so he could dive as often as he liked. Harel the Bone Gull, carved by Ennu the winter the boats lay on the shingle, sits to the south and watches the diving, for want of other work. Nethe the Drying Shag, up in the north-east, waits on her black rock for the sun to dry her, and will not go in. Hesk wrote it down: one dive, one salt. Haku still goes down every autumn, and still comes up with only the sea.
output.finding: Start at Harel, the Bone Gull, and go a fist and a third due north (about 13°) to find Haku.
